title: BlobIntegrityMismatch field names are backwards in error message
description: error.rs: ClientError::BlobIntegrityMismatch has fields 'expected' and 'actual'. In upload_blob (blob.rs line 176-179), 'expected' is set to server_lower (the server's reported hash) and 'actual' is set to local_sha256 (what we computed locally). In download_blob (line 261-264), 'expected' is set to expected_lower (the hash the caller passed in) and 'actual' is set to the locally-computed hash of the downloaded bytes. This naming is inconsistent between the two call sites: for upload, 'expected' means 'what the server said' (not what the caller expected); for download, 'expected' means 'what the caller said'. The error message reads 'blob integrity check failed: expected {expected}, got {actual}' — for upload this translates to 'expected [server hash], got [local hash]', which reads backwards to a user who is thinking about what they uploaded. The convention should be: 'expected' = what the local computation produced (the ground truth), 'actual' = what the remote said. This will generate recurring bug reports from users who see the error and misdiagnose which side is wrong.
